title: Quiet Errands
tagline: A neighbour is missing, and the trail starts with three small jobs.
opening: Someone from the nearest village vanished three nights ago, and nobody will say why. The only clues are small ones. Follow them before the trail goes cold.
ending: You found who was behind it and stopped them. The village sleeps safely tonight, and they know who to thank.

steps.tell: The missing neighbour was last seen gathering supplies in {area}. Collect what they left behind. It may show where they went.
aftermath: A half-eaten loaf, a lantern still warm, a boot print that is not theirs. Someone was here, and they were not alone.

steps.tell: Their trail leads to a place in {area}. Go and look. Something happened there that the villagers are afraid to talk about.
aftermath: The villagers were right to be afraid. The ground is scorched in a ring, and the ring is not natural. Something is hunting.

steps.tell: Whatever took them is still in {area}, and it will take someone else next. Defeat it now.
aftermath: Behind it lies a torn sleeve in the neighbour's own stitching. They walked away from here alive. The village should hear it.

title: The Long Road
tagline: The only trade road is cut. Reopen it before winter.
opening: The trade road has been cut for weeks, and the villages at the far end are running out of food. Someone has to clear it, stop by stop, before winter closes in.
ending: The road is open again. Carts are already rolling, and the far villages will eat this winter because of you.

steps.tell: The first stop is {area}. Nobody has come back from there in weeks. Find out why.
aftermath: The milestones are smashed and the ruts are fresh. This was no accident of weather. Someone wants this road dead.

steps.tell: Raiders took over the road in {area}. Defeat them, or no cart will ever get through.
aftermath: Among the raiders' things, a ledger of every cart that dared to pass. They were paid by the cart. Someone far off kept count.

steps.tell: The road crews need supplies to rebuild it. Gather them in {area}.
aftermath: The crews' hammers ring for the first time in weeks. A road is only a promise that someone will keep it open.

steps.tell: The last blocked stretch is in {area}, where the road crews buried their tools. Find them so the road can be finished.
aftermath: The tools lie oiled and wrapped under the dirt. The crews hid them well. They always meant to come back.

title: The Great Hunt
tagline: Something is driving the beasts mad. Trace it to its source.
opening: Beasts that never used to attack villages are suddenly raiding them, as if something is driving them. If nobody finds the cause, the next raid reaches a town.
ending: The source is destroyed and the beasts are calm again. The villages are safe, and the hunters will remember what you did.

steps.tell: The raids start here in {area}. Defeat the beasts and watch which way the survivors run.
aftermath: The survivors do not scatter. They run in a line, all one way, like beads on a string. Something is pulling the string.

steps.tell: The survivors fled to {area} and are angrier there. Stop them before they reach the villages.
aftermath: These beasts are thin, and their eyes are wrong. They are not hunting. They are fleeing, and what they flee is behind you now.

steps.tell: Whatever is driving them is close, in {area}. Defeat the beasts guarding it.
aftermath: The guards fall, and the air changes. Quiet, then a sound like a slow heartbeat from further on. Whatever it is, it is awake.

steps.tell: Their trail ends in {area}. Go there and end this.

title: A Harvest Against the Dark
tagline: The winter food is still in the fields, and something is hunting the gatherers.
opening: The villages have no winter food unless the last crops are gathered this week, but something has started hunting the gatherers. Bring the harvest in, and protect it.
ending: The harvest is in, and the villages will have enough to last until spring.

steps.tell: Start in {area}. The nearest crops are there. Gather as much as you can carry.
aftermath: Baskets full, hands raw. Along the fence, deep claw marks, and the crows have gone quiet. Something is watching the field.

steps.tell: Something is stalking the gatherers in {area}. Defeat it before it kills someone.
aftermath: It was thin, and starved. The last rows behind it are untouched. It could have fed on them, and did not. Odd, for a monster.

steps.tell: There is more food in {area}, past where the stalker hid. Gather it and finish the harvest.

title: The Lost Relics
tagline: Three old treasures could pay for a village to rebuild. Find them.
opening: A village burned down last spring and cannot afford to rebuild. Three old treasures are hidden in three different lands, and together they could pay for everything. Find them before treasure hunters do.
ending: All three treasures are found, and the village will be rebuilt.

steps.tell: The first treasure is hidden in {area}. Search the area for it.
aftermath: Wrapped in oilcloth and a child's blanket. Whoever hid it loved it, and meant to come back. Two treasures remain.

steps.tell: The second treasure is in {area}. It is buried deeper, so search carefully.
aftermath: It lay under a cairn built with care, the stones still warm from the day. You are not the first to look, only the first to dig.

steps.tell: The third and last treasure is in {area}. Find it before anyone else does.

title: Pilgrimage to the Far Shrine
tagline: A dying elder wants to see the far shrine. Clear the way for the pilgrimage.
opening: The village elder is dying and has one wish: to see the far shrine once more. The route is long and dangerous. Go ahead of the pilgrims and make it safe for them.
ending: The shrine is open and the way is safe. The elder will make the trip, thanks to you.

steps.tell: The pilgrimage starts at {area}. Go there and make sure the way is passable.
aftermath: The road is passable, if the pilgrims keep a patient pace. Somewhere ahead, a bell tolls for no reason anyone can name.

steps.tell: Next is {area}. It is a longer walk than it looks, so scout it before the pilgrims arrive.
aftermath: Cold ashes, and prayer ribbons tied to a dead branch. Other pilgrims passed this way, and did not stay.

steps.tell: Then {area}. Other scouts turned back here. Do not.
aftermath: A scout's pack lies here with his journal. The last line: 'Turned back at the third marker. I wish I had not looked up.'

steps.tell: Enemies guard the shrine in {area}. Defeat them so the pilgrims can reach it.

title: The Siege of the Frontier
tagline: Raiders are besieging the frontier. Break the siege before supplies run out.
opening: Raiders have besieged the frontier settlement, and its food will last only days. Break the siege, then find out who is leading the raiders.
ending: The siege is broken and the raiders scattered. The settlement is free, and they will not forget who saved them.

steps.tell: The first raiding party is in {area}. Defeat it before it reaches the settlement.
aftermath: The raiders carried oil, rope and a map with the settlement circled in red. This was no mob. It was a plan.

steps.tell: The settlement is running out of food. Gather supplies in {area} and bring them back.
aftermath: The gate opens for you, then shuts. Children watch from the rooftops. The siege has been counting days, and so have they.

steps.tell: A second raiding party is forming in {area}. Strike before it is ready.
aftermath: The raiders scatter, and their torch smoke drifts toward one point on the horizon: where their leaders wait.

steps.tell: The raid leaders are in {area}. Defeat them and the raiders will break.
aftermath: The leaders fall. One wears a cloak with a crest nobody here recognises, and everyone here fears.

steps.tell: The leaders dropped something they came here for. Search {area} for it so they cannot come back for it.

title: Beyond the Edge of the Map
tagline: Map the farthest lands before the cartographers give up on them.
opening: The cartographers say the farthest lands are empty, and will stop paying for expeditions unless someone brings proof. Travel to the edge of the map and bring back evidence.
ending: You reached the farthest land and came back with proof. The expedition will be funded again.

steps.tell: Go to {area}, where the known map begins to thin out.
aftermath: The road ends in waist-high grass, and the map ends with it. Past this, the compass needle trembles like a nervous hand.

steps.tell: Gather plants that only grow in {area}. They are the proof the cartographers want.
aftermath: The plants smell of rain and iron and nothing you know. The cartographers will pay well, and will not quite believe you.

steps.tell: Something lives in {area} and does not welcome visitors. Defeat it.
aftermath: It lies still, a sliver of carved bone in its claws. Someone made that mark. Someone lived out here once.

steps.tell: Search the edge of {area} for a marker left by the first explorers. It proves they were here.

title: The Hollow Crown
tagline: Thieves stole the royal crown. Follow them and bring it back.
opening: The royal crown was stolen from the king last week. Without it he cannot rule, and rival lords are already moving. Follow the thieves across the lands and recover it.
ending: The crown is recovered and the thieves are finished. The king keeps his throne, and he owes you.

steps.tell: The thieves hid a piece of the regalia in {area}. They thought nobody would look there. Search for it.
aftermath: A gem-studded circlet, snapped in two. They are selling the crown in pieces. Time is shorter than the king believes.

steps.tell: The thieves have a camp in {area}. Defeat them and take back what they stole.
aftermath: In the camp's ashes, a letter under a noble's seal. The thieves did not steal this for gold. They were hired.

steps.tell: Their trail leads to {area}. Go there and see who they work for.
aftermath: The trail ends at a gate with a banner you have seen before, on the king's own hall wall. Someone near the throne wanted it empty.

steps.tell: There are too many guards in {area} to sneak past. Defeat them.
aftermath: The guards fall, and one wears the king's livery under his stolen cloak. There is a traitor at court.

steps.tell: The crown itself is hidden in {area}. Search for it, and bring it home.

title: The Lost Courier
tagline: A sealed letter, three strangers and a message that must arrive.
opening: A letter was given to a courier, and the courier never arrived. Somebody, somewhere, is still waiting for it. Let us see who.
ending: The letter reached the hand it was meant for, and the world is a little less lost for it.

postmaster.name: Aldis the Postmaster
lines: No courier has come through in days. I fear the worst.
If you find the letter, do not open it.
after: You found the courier? Thank the stars. I will not send another on that road alone.
finished: The letter arrived! I have had word. You have the thanks of the whole post.

courier.name: Wren the Courier
lines: I ran. I am not proud of it, but I ran.
Take the letter. Take it to the one it was meant for.
after: I am no longer afraid of that road. Not with the letter in good hands.
finished: I ride again tomorrow. Perhaps I will tell the tale of the day strangers saved my route.

reader.name: Sage Orrin
lines: Letters from the old road. Rare, these days.
Whoever sent this knew more than they wrote.
after: I have read it twice now. It says more than I care to repeat.
finished: Come back one day. I will have a good deal more to tell you.

steps.tell: The postmaster in {area} is beside himself. Find Aldis, and hear what happened.
says: A courier left here three days ago with a sealed letter, and has not been seen since.
She was last bound for the lands beyond. Find her, if you can, and the letter with her.

steps.tell: Whatever stopped the courier is still out there in {area}. Clear the road before you follow it.
aftermath: The road is clear. In the mud, small hurried footprints leave it and run. Someone fled this place, and fled well.

steps.tell: A frightened traveller is hiding in {area}. Find Wren the courier.
says: You came for the letter. Good. I could not carry it another step.
It is for the old sage who keeps the lore. Please, see it into their hands.

steps.tell: The sage the letter is for lives in {area}. Carry the Sealed Letter there and give it over.
says: Ah. So it has come at last. You have done more than you know.
What it says is not for you, but this I will tell you: the roads will be safer for it.

title: The Silent Bell
tagline: A bell that stopped ringing, a keeper with a secret, a trail to follow.
opening: There was a bell in the lands that rang every dusk. It has gone silent, and the silence has begun to spread.
ending: The bell rang again at dusk, and everyone who heard it knew the long silence was over.

ringer.name: Old Maren the Ringer
lines: Forty years I rang that bell. Now there is only quiet.
Find what took the clapper, and bring it home.
after: You have the clapper? Then there is hope for my bell yet.
finished: Did you hear it ring? Forty years, and I wept like a child. Thank you.

smith.name: Dorrin Ashhand
lines: I mend what breaks, but I cannot mend what is missing.
Bring me the clapper and the bell will sing.
after: It rings true now. Take care of it, and take care of each other.
finished: I heard the bell from here this dusk. It made the whole forge feel lighter.

steps.tell: The bell-ringer in {area} has a sorrow to tell. Find Old Maren.
says: The bell hangs there still, but its voice is gone. The clapper was taken in the night.
Whoever took it left tracks heading out. Follow them.

steps.tell: The tracks end in {area}. The clapper is hidden somewhere near. Search the land until you have it.
aftermath: Cold iron wrapped in sacking: the clapper, scored with teeth. Something chewed the bell's own voice before it ran.

steps.tell: Whatever carried it off has made its den in {area}, and it will not give the clapper up without a fight.
aftermath: It gives up the clapper with its last breath. Perhaps it only wanted to hear the sound it made. Bells are loud, and the dark is lonely.

steps.tell: Take the clapper to the smith in {area}. Find Dorrin Ashhand.
says: A fine piece, and nearly whole. Give me a moment at the anvil.
There. Carry it back to the bell, and may it ring true.

steps.tell: The bell hangs where it always did, in {area}. Return the clapper to it, and let it ring.

title: The Wanderer's Debt
tagline: A stranger owes a favour to someone he has never met, and you are the road between.
opening: A wanderer on the road owes a debt he cannot pay. Perhaps you can pay it for him, and learn something on the way.
ending: The debt is paid, the wanderer is free, and two strangers parted as friends.

wanderer.name: Corwin the Wanderer
lines: I owe someone a debt, and I do not even know their face.
They live beyond the next land, so I am told.
after: You have the coins? Then I am a free man, or near enough.
finished: The debt is paid, and I am lighter for it. Whatever road you take, I wish you a kinder one.

creditor.name: Keeper Hale
lines: A debt? I had forgotten it entirely.
Odd, to be repaid by strangers.
after: Odd to be repaid by strangers, but I will not refuse a good deed.
finished: Corwin sat at my fire last night. I did not know a debt could make a friend.

steps.tell: A traveller in {area} is looking for help with a debt. Find Corwin.
says: Take these coins, friends. They are what I owe, and a little more.
The one I owe lives some way off. Please, find them. I cannot.

steps.tell: On the road to the creditor, {area} offers what a gift ought to have beside it. Gather it as you pass.
aftermath: The gifts are light, but the road to the creditor feels heavy. Some debts are paid in more than coin.

steps.tell: The creditor is in {area}. Find Keeper Hale, and settle the debt.
says: These are the old coins, aren't they? My grandmother's pouch.
Tell Corwin the debt is paid, and something more besides. He is welcome at my fire.

title: The Innkeeper's Worry
tagline: A quiet inn, an empty room and a guest who left without paying or saying goodbye.
opening: The innkeeper has kept a room for a regular guest for twenty years. This season the guest never came, and the innkeeper cannot sleep for worrying.
ending: The old guest is found, well and only lost in grief. The room at the inn is aired, and a lamp burns in its window again.

innkeeper.name: Mother Brannagh
lines: Twenty years, and never once late. Something is wrong, I can feel it.
Sit, eat. Then go and look for him, if you would.
after: Any word? I keep his room aired, every morning.
finished: He is coming back for the winter. Your supper is on the house, tonight and every night.

pilgrim.name: Old Tobin
lines: Leave me be. I am only resting.
My wife walked this road with me every year. This year I walk it alone.
after: Tell Brannagh I am well. Tell her I will come when I can face the room.
finished: I went back to the inn. It was easier than I feared.

steps.tell: The innkeeper in {area} has a worry she will tell to anyone who sits a while. Find Mother Brannagh.
says: My oldest guest walks the far road every year, and every year he stays here. Not this year.
He always stops at the same places on the way. Start where the road leaves us.

steps.tell: The old guest always rested in {area} on his way. Walk there and look about for any sign of him.
aftermath: The old guest's chair stands empty and his cup is full of rainwater. He has not left this place in some time.

steps.tell: A grey-bearded traveller sits alone in {area}, and has done for days. Find Old Tobin.
says: She found me, then. Brannagh always does.
Take this flower to her. She will know what it means, and why I am late.

steps.tell: Carry the Pressed Flower back to Mother Brannagh at the inn in {area}, and tell her what you found.
says: A pressed flower. He gave me one every spring, the first year we kept this room.
Then he is well, and only lost in grief. Thank you. Go and rest; your supper is on me.

title: Market Day
tagline: The big market is in three days, and half the stalls have nothing to sell.
opening: Market day is when the whole valley comes to town, and this year the stalls are bare. The merchants say the roads are bad. The townsfolk say the merchants are lazy. Somebody has to find out.
ending: Market day came, the stalls were full, and the town sang until dawn. The merchants have not stopped telling people who saved it.

merchant.name: Pella Quickcoin
lines: Bare stalls, and the market in three days. I will be ruined.
My goods are stuck somewhere on the road. I would pay well to know where.
after: Is that my wagon's mark? Then it is out there still.
finished: Best market in ten years. If you ever need anything, it is half price for you.

carter.name: Big Ansel
lines: A wheel broke, and then the ox wandered off. It has been a week like that.
I am not going anywhere until somebody helps me.
after: Off you go. I will have the wagon in town by market day, I promise.
finished: We made it with an hour to spare. I owe you a cart ride, any time.

smith.name: Hilde the Smith
lines: Broken wheel? Bring me the iron and I will mend it before supper.
Anything worth doing is worth a fair price.
after: There, a rim that will outlast the wagon. Take it to your carter.
finished: Market day, and my hammer has not stopped. Good for business, you lot.

steps.tell: A merchant in {area} is pacing beside an empty stall. Find Pella Quickcoin and hear her out.
says: My wagon left the far farms a week ago. It should have been here by now.
Follow the road out. If my carter is in a ditch, I want to know.

steps.tell: A big man is sitting beside a lopsided wagon in {area}. Find Big Ansel.
says: The wheel rim cracked clean through. I need a smith, and I cannot leave the goods.
Take the broken rim to a smith, and quick. Market day will not wait.

steps.tell: Carry the broken rim to the smith in {area}. Find Hilde.
says: Cracked by a stone, by the look of it. Give me a moment at the forge.
There. Run it back to your carter before the light goes.

steps.tell: While the wheel is fitted, Ansel asks for something to pack around the goods in {area}. Gather it, and the wagon can roll.
aftermath: The wagon creaks, then rolls. The stalls will be full by noon, and nobody will remember who made it so, except you.

title: Stone and Steel
tagline: A gem in the pack is only a pebble until it is set in something.
opening: A stone that stays in a pack is a stone wasted. A smith knows better, and so, soon, will you.
ending: You set the stone, tried the edge and found it keen. The smith will tell the story for years, with a few embellishments of their own.

steps.tell: Set a gem in a good piece of gear, from the Inventory tab, and see what a little patience makes of it. {area} is as fine a place to do it as any.
aftermath: The gem sits in its setting as if it were always meant to. A little patience, and a plain thing turns fine.

steps.tell: A new piece wants trying. Take it into {area} and let something with opinions see what it can do.
aftermath: It cuts true, and gleams when it should not. The smith would be pleased, and a little smug.

steps.tell: Word of fine work travels faster than the worker. Show yours in {area}, where someone has already been asking after it.

title: The Drowned Choir
tagline: At night the dead of the old well sing. Someone is teaching them new songs.
opening: Every night the dead of the old well sing, and every night they sing a little more words. The choir mistress says the new words are a name. Hers.
ending: The well is quiet. For the first time in a month, the village slept through, and the choir mistress sang the old hymn on her own.

mistress.name: Isolde the Choir Mistress
lines: I know every voice in this valley. The ones from the well are learning from me.
Find who is leading them, before they finish my name.
after: A bell-ringer's apprentice, you say? Then he never stopped rehearsing.
finished: The well is quiet. I sang the old hymn alone tonight, and it was enough.

ferryman.name: Tam Ferryman
lines: I carry the living across and the dead stay put. That was the bargain, until lately.
The one who breaks bargains has a lantern. Look for the light.
after: Take the lantern to the well and set it down. Then run.
finished: Quiet water again. Funny. I almost miss the singing.

steps.tell: The choir mistress in {area} has not slept in a week. Find Isolde, and hear what the well has been singing.
says: They sing at midnight, a little more every night. Last night they sang 'Isolde'.
Somebody taught them. Find the ferryman at the crossing. He knows who walks there.
aftermath: A name sung by the dead is a name spoken twice. The ferryman will know who started it.

steps.tell: The ferryman at the crossing in {area} knows who walks by night. Find Tam, and ask him plainly.
says: A young man with a lantern, three nights a week. He pays in old coins and never speaks.
He dug where the village buried its bad harvests. Find what he left there.
aftermath: Old coins, an unspoken name and a lantern at midnight. The ferryman's story is a very tidy one, and tidy stories are usually stitched.

steps.tell: Whatever answers the lantern gathers in {area}. Put down the ones that came to the call, before the call grows louder.
aftermath: Where they fell, a ring of pale candle stubs, all burned to the same height. Whoever made this had patience, and a plan.

steps.tell: The lantern's keeper left his notes in {area}, buried with the candles. Dig until you have them.
aftermath: His notes name a crown of reeds, a ledger of drownings, and one line underlined twice: 'She will lead them better than I ever could.'

steps.tell: He is waiting in {area}, where the choir is loudest, and he knows you are coming. Stop the singing at its source.
aftermath: The last note fades. A lantern falls and goes out, and across the valley a well finally holds its tongue.

title: The Cartographer's Last Map
tagline: A dying mapmaker left one chart unfinished. Whatever it shows, it is not on any other map.
opening: A cartographer died last winter with one map unfinished, three marks inked and the fourth only pencilled. His apprentice swears the marks are real. Nobody else believes it.
ending: The fourth mark is drawn at last, in your hand, in ink. The apprentice cried, and then drew the map's name in the corner: yours.

apprentice.name: Fenn the Apprentice
lines: Master Corvin left four marks and no key. I have the first three nights of his notes.
Each mark is a place that should not be where he drew it.
after: The marks match his notes. He was not mad. He was early.
finished: I finished the map. The fourth mark is yours, and so is its name.

steps.tell: Corvin's apprentice keeps the unfinished map in {area}. Find Fenn, and see the marks for yourself.
says: The first mark is near. The second, past the second land. The third and the fourth, I have not dared guess.
Visit the first. If the land matches the ink, we are not fools.
aftermath: The first mark is a small black cross over a place you know well. Nobody ever drew it there. Somebody should have.

steps.tell: The first mark is set in {area}. Go there, and see whether the land matches the ink.
aftermath: The land matches to the stone. A dead map-maker knew a place better than the people who live beside it. Uncomfortable, that.

steps.tell: Master Corvin's notes say the second mark hides plants that make ink dry blue. Gather them in {area} for the apprentice.
aftermath: Blue ink, fresh from the stalk. On parchment it shows a faint line that was invisible before: a road, leading on.

steps.tell: The third mark sits in {area}, and something has made its home on it. Clear it out, so the map can be read.
aftermath: On the third mark, a cairn, and under it Corvin's own compass, still pointing the way. He came here once. He was not alone.

steps.tell: His journal's last pages are buried somewhere in {area}. Search until the apprentice has the whole story.
aftermath: The last page reads: 'The fourth mark is where I turned back. Whoever finishes this, forgive me, and forgive what waits there.'

steps.tell: The fourth mark is in {area}, and what waits there is the reason a mapmaker stopped. Go and finish his map.
aftermath: It falls, and the silence after is the kind that only comes at the very end of a map.

title: The Wolf Under the Hill
tagline: The shepherds say a wolf is taking sheep. The sheep say otherwise.
opening: Three shepherds swear a monster takes their sheep. The sheep come home fat and calm. Someone is lying, and the one with the sharpest teeth has the best excuse.
ending: The wolf is still under the hill, and the sheep still come home fat. The shepherds pay the real thieves now, and the wolf asks nothing.

shepherd.name: Old Bram the Shepherd
lines: Three sheep this week. A wolf, plain as day, and a big one.
Hunt it down, and I will pay you in wool and thanks.
after: Not a wolf? Then who is dressing in its skin? I'll have a word with them.
finished: I owe that wolf an apology, and a good lamb. I will bring it both.

girl.name: Little Wynn
lines: He is not a bad wolf. He minds the sheep when Da is drunk.
The ones who take them wear boots. I have seen the boots.
after: Tell Da. He will not hear it from me. He never does.
finished: The wolf waved at me today. I know wolves do not wave. He did.

steps.tell: Bram's flock grazes in {area}. Find the shepherd, and hear about the wolf.
says: A big grey wolf, lair under the hill. Takes a sheep a night, and cheeky with it.
Kill it, and the valley sleeps. Go and find where it hides.
aftermath: The shepherd is certain, which in your experience is when to start looking at the evidence.

steps.tell: Beasts have gathered about the lair in {area}. Thin them out until you can reach the wolf's den.
aftermath: No sheep bones, no blood. A hunting beast would leave both. Whatever lives here does not eat what it guards.

steps.tell: A child watches from the hillside in {area}. Find Wynn, who has something to say about the wolf.
says: He is not a bad wolf. He guards the sheep when Da is asleep.
The thieves wear boots. They come by night, from the old quarry.
aftermath: Boots and a quarry. The wolf is not the thief. He is the only witness who cannot testify.

steps.tell: The real thieves operate from {area}. Strike before the next night, and the sheep keep their guardian.
aftermath: Among their things, a half-finished ledger: so many sheep to a trade, so many wolf-pelts for the wolf's reputation.

steps.tell: Return to {area}, and stand at the wolf's hill so the valley sees you did not raise a blade against him.
aftermath: The wolf watches you from the ridge, and lowers its head. Some thanks do not need words, or a lamb.

title: The Tithe of Bones
tagline: A plague doctor offers a cure. The tithe is the village's dead.
opening: A plague doctor came to the dying village with a cure, and a price: one bone from every grave. The village paid. The sickness stayed, and the graves are empty.
ending: The doctor's mask lies cracked on the road, and the bones are home again. The village buried them once more, with better prayers, and names carved properly this time.

priest.name: Brother Alder
lines: I blessed every grave myself. Now I do not know what I blessed.
The doctor sells hope and takes bones. Find where he takes them.
after: Then it is as I feared. He is not a doctor. He is a collector.
finished: Every bone is home. I said the names, and I did not need the book.

gravedigger.name: Hobb Gravedigger
lines: Forty years I put them in. Never once did I take one out. Until this week.
Somebody dug from below, I tell you. From below.
after: Under the old crypt, you say? Then someone has been tunnelling for months.
finished: I put every one back myself. Slowly. They deserved the care.

steps.tell: The village priest in {area} no longer trusts his own graveyard. Find Brother Alder, and hear what the doctor took.
says: He came with a cure and a tithe: one bone per grave. We paid. The fever stayed.
Ask the gravedigger what he found. He has not spoken in days.
aftermath: A tithe of bones for a cure that does not cure. The doctor's bargain was never medicine. It was inventory.

steps.tell: The gravedigger keeps to {area}, beside his tools. Find Hobb, and hear it from the ground up.
says: The graves were opened from below, not above. Tunnels, neat as a mine.
Follow them. Where they end, the bones are being counted.
aftermath: Tunnels under a churchyard, dug from below, neat as a mine. Whoever is counting bones has done this before.

steps.tell: The tunnels surface in {area}, and what guards them is not alive. Put the guards down.
aftermath: The guards were the village's own dead, wearing the doctor's mark. Whatever he is, he is building something out of the people he failed.

steps.tell: The doctor's ledger of bones, village by village, is hidden in {area}. Find it, and learn how many places he has done this.
aftermath: The ledger lists forty villages. Thirty-nine have a line through them. This one does not. Yet.

steps.tell: His workroom in {area} is full of reagents that keep the dead from resting. Gather them so nobody can use them again.
aftermath: The bottles smell of old graves and sweet decay. Burned, they make a smoke that hangs in the air like a prayer, and it is a good one.

steps.tell: The doctor waits in {area}, among everything he collected. End the tithe before the last grave is opened.
aftermath: His mask falls, and there is nothing under it but a sheet of vellum with a name on it. It is a very old name.
